pr_body:
This PR extends: https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/18769

to fix https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/18547

The stored LoginName was not used for existing accounts. 

I'm no gitea expert, so the fix may not be optimal. I'll try to figure out if we can add this in a unit test tomorrow, any guidance would be useful.

For clarity, this has been tested and solves the issue that it is no longer possible to login when a different loginname is stored.

I have tested both your PR https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/18769 and https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/18786

They do not fix the issue.

both do not work because the loginname for ldap is different from the email or the username in this case.

OK. Look at the error log
```
2022/02/17 23:29:05 ...dap/source_search.go:98:findUserDN() [D] Failed search using filter[(&(objectclass=posixAccount)(uid=johanvdw))]: <nil>
```
It should search different field per requested login name. If it's an email, search `mail `, if it's not an email, just search `uid`.
I just sent another PR #18800, but it should also not fix your problem. Your problem is that the user you login `johanvdw` and `johan@fluves.com` haven't been synchronized into Gitea's user table.
#18800 is another PR should partially fix this.

> OK. Look at the error log
> 
> ```
> 2022/02/17 23:29:05 ...dap/source_search.go:98:findUserDN() [D] Failed search using filter[(&(objectclass=posixAccount)(uid=johanvdw))]: <nil>
> ```
> 
> It should search different field per requested login name. If it's an email, search `mail `, if it's not an email, just search `uid`.

No, the issue was that the username passed in the loginbox ("johanvdw") was passed, rather than the loginName stored for the user. My PR fixed that. I don't think it is a syncing issue. This login worked before, no recent changes were done to it.

With my fix applied, logging in works again as before. I can use both email and gitea username to login.

As I understand it , #18800 is actually the same fix that was applied previously in my PR(https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/18789/files#diff-61ff4979f4806bfe43709f4004297c6366b2baeb9fdf73e5c201d7ecd6b4beef) , except not specific to ldap. If it is fixed at that level, we probably can undo that change.

```
2022/02/17 23:31:19 ...dap/source_search.go:98:findUserDN() [D] Failed search using filter[(&(objectclass=posixAccount)(uid=johan@fluves.com))]: <nil>
```
I think I'm wrong. As above there is a situation that when a ldap user login with email but his account didn't sync to Gitea. Then Gitea will find user with email address.

Another issue I found - maybe:

The LDAP search searches the user by its LoginName - so far so good. But after that, the system checks, if the user exists with the `sr` Username. And I had one case, in which Username and LogiName is different.

https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/main/services/auth/source/ldap/source_authenticate.go#L36

The existence check should use the provided `user`, if present. So, for me a different LogiName (compared to Username) has no functionality. User and LoginName have to be the same in this case.

Can someone confirm or clearify that?
Please fire another issue.

review_comments: I think userName should not be empty? It should be come from inputbox.

But the username may be different from the loginname that must be used with ldap. It could also be an email address. 

In ldap you want to search for the login name only (this was at least what was working up to version 1.15.9).
So that should be changed in the progress of LDAP users sync but not when authenticating. When sync a user, we need to know should we use login name as identify or use email?

I still think this is the appropriate place - when you login using your gitea username or email address, validation must be done using the loginname that was stored for the account. 

I improved wording a bit in a new commit.

OK. Let's clarify. If `user` is nil, that means there is no user found in Gitea's table, `userName` is input by login user, it could be a name or an email address. So if `user` is nil, and `userName` is email. This function will return failure.

Of course, this resolved the problem when `user` is not nil and `userName` is email. I think we can merge it at first.
